# TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build — facts

> Source-anchored units about TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build: 12 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-29 · 12 units · 6 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Apple TN3127 documents codesign --display -r - <app> as a way to inspect an app’s designated requirement. Inspect the exact App Store Connect or TestFlight app under investigation because a development-signed variant can carry a different requirement from the store-distributed variant. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3127-inside-code-signing-requirements · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/en.lproj/dev31de635e5.html
- [statement] Apple’s notarization documentation says software distributed through the Mac App Store does not require separate notarization because App Store submission includes equivalent security checks. The electron-builder Mac App Store guide reports the same split between store distribution and direct Developer ID distribution. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://www.electron.build/docs/mas/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] The original Mac App Store distribution-signed archive is not a supported general-purpose local launch artifact. Apple says macOS may sometimes run it, but this is unsupported and can fail when the app claims restricted entitlements. Apple identifies TestFlight as a pre-release testing route because it re-signs the app. This separates uploading the archive from running the TestFlight-installed copy. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3161-inside-code-signing-certificates?changes=__8 · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/qa/qa1884/_index.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A designated requirement (DR) is the code identity test embedded in a signature, and macOS can use it to recognize the same code during later authorization checks. Apple documents `codesign -d -r- <app>` as a way to display the DR. Apple also says TestFlight re-signs an app for testing; therefore, inspect the installed TestFlight artifact itself rather than treating the pre-upload archive's DR as conclusive (the last sentence is an inference from Apple's re-signing description). (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3127-inside-code-signing-requirements · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/technotes/tn2206/_index.html, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3161-inside-code-signing-certificates?changes=__8
- [statement] Apple TN3127 says an Apple Development designated requirement differs from the requirements used by Developer ID and Mac App Store apps; it explicitly says a Mac App Store app will not satisfy the Apple Development requirement, or vice versa. Apple’s code requirements guide says codesign typically derives a default designated requirement from the program name and signature chain when the signer supplies no explicit requirement. (high confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3127-inside-code-signing-requirements · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/applying-code-requirements?changes=__3_3&language=objc

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Apple's current Xcode guide groups TestFlight and App Store delivery under App Store Connect and says that channel uses an Apple Developer Program distribution provisioning profile. Apple also says TestFlight re-signs the app much like the App Store. Do not treat the local pre-upload Apple Distribution identity as a complete description of the delivered TestFlight artifact. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-29) — https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/en.lproj/dev31de635e5.html · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3161-inside-code-signing-certificates?changes=__8
- [statement] A sample `spctl --list` output in the PyOxidizer Apple code-signing guide labels a `[Testflight]` rule `allow execute` and lists separate `[Mac App Store]` rules for `allow install` and `allow execute`. This is sample policy output, not a guarantee that current macOS releases use the same labels or requirements. (low confidence) — https://pyoxidizer.readthedocs.io/_/downloads/en/apple-codesign-0.15.0/pdf/ · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build
- [statement] Apple’s DTS Gatekeeper troubleshooting guidance focuses on Developer ID-signed code and recommends strict codesign verification; it says Gatekeeper should not block App Store apps. A separate third-party release audit says its signature, notarization, and stapling checks did not install the package. Implementation inference for TestFlight: inspect the delivered beta’s signature and designated requirement and test its actual launch separately, without assuming Developer ID Gatekeeper guidance applies unchanged. (medium confidence) — https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/706379 · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/technotes/tn2206/_index.html, https://github.com/scholay/rimes/blob/main/validation/release-audit-20261007.md
- [statement] A 2024 electron-builder issue reports that an app installed through TestFlight failed to launch. The author said a Developer ID installer package passed notarization but failed Transporter validation, while a Mac App Store installer package passed Transporter but failed notarization. The author later reported success after enabling electron-builder’s notarization option and expressed a belief that it notarized the app before packaging. This is one self-reported workflow result and does not establish that all TestFlight builds require notarization. (low confidence) — https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/8382 · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build
- [statement] Xcode documents App Store Connect as the distribution method for apps delivered through TestFlight or the App Store, signed with an Apple Developer Program distribution provisioning profile. The electron-builder Mac App Store guide identifies Mac App Distribution as the app signing certificate and Mac Installer Distribution as the uploaded package certificate. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/en.lproj/dev31de635e5.html · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://www.electron.build/docs/mas/
- [statement] Apple’s Xcode launch simulation uses spctl -a -v and quarantined copies for Developer ID-signed apps. Mac Hardening’s September 2026 guide says Mac App Store apps report their own spctl source and that a rejected result predicts rejection if the app were quarantined. Do not treat a Developer ID notarization result as the expected Gatekeeper label for a TestFlight build. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://help.apple.com/xcode/mac/current/en.lproj/dev1cc22a95c.html · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://www.machardening.com/en/blog/gatekeeper-xprotect-notarization, https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution
- [statement] In electron-builder issue 8382, the author reported that a Developer ID installer package passed notarization but failed Transporter checks, while a Mac App Store installer package passed Transporter but failed notarization. The author later reported resolving the case by enabling electron-builder’s notarization option and said they believed it notarized the app before packaging. This self-report illustrates separate validation outcomes; it does not establish that a TestFlight build needs Developer ID notarization. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/electron-userland/electron-builder/issues/8382 · keywords: TestFlight designated requirement and Gatekeeper launch of a store-signed Mac build · also: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/security/notarizing-macos-software-before-distribution
